purpose: Gate Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B on the same BGE-M3 hybrid r100 Arabic MIRACL top-100 candidate pool before deciding whether to run a full rerank.
research_basis: The Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B model card lists sentence-transformers CrossEncoder usage as an official path.
The same model card also provides a transformers AutoModelForCausalLM yes/no scoring path and recommends English task instructions in multilingual contexts.
Because the v47 BGE-reranker-v2-m3 full run improved the frozen BGE-M3 hybrid candidate pool, any Qwen reranker must first beat the same-query 200-query gate before scaling.

v48_cross_encoder.prompt: Given an Arabic search query, retrieve relevant Arabic passages that answer the query.

v49_qwen3_causal.prompt: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query

decision: Do not scale Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B to full dev. Both the CrossEncoder wrapper and the official causal yes/no path underperformed the same first-stage candidate ordering on the identical 200-query gate.
interpretation: Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B is a strong public reranker family member, but this specific small reranker did not improve the Arabic MIRACL BGE-M3 hybrid top-100 candidate ordering under either tested inference path.
The causal backend was better than the CrossEncoder wrapper on this sample, but it still lost to the frozen first-stage ordering by -0.034985 nDCG@10.
The negative result strengthens the decision to use v47 BGE-reranker-v2-m3 as the current best teacher rather than chasing Qwen3-0.6B full reranking.
next_experiment: Use the v47 BGE-reranker-v2-m3 ordering as the teacher for a trainable student, or run a separate gated Qwen3-Reranker-4B probe only if the project budget accepts a much slower cross-encoder sample.
